problems: The blind guess (a swan or water bird with a raised neck) does not match the intended subject, The Bailer (a handled bowl with a spout and water drops). The figure reads as a bailer, so the drawing is working, but a viewer would not identify it unaided.

Labels collide on the right side: 'right wall of the bowl' runs into 'spout lip tip', and 'upper-left rim of the bowl,' and 'left wall of the bowl' sit close together, which makes the mapping of stars to parts hard to read.
The bowl is narrow and its walls are not clearly distinguished from the handle arch, so the cup shape is weak. The handle, bowl and spout are present and in the right order.

The figure is upright: the handle knob is at the top, the bowl is in the middle, the spout points right and the water drops fall below it. The gold path follows the key stars in the right order (knob, arch apex, rim, left wall, base, right wall, spout tip, drops).
The blue outline is a thin double-line trace rather than a filled silhouette, so the shape reads more as a wire outline than a solid form.
output.advice: Redraw so the bailer's silhouette reads clearly as a cup with a handle. Widen the bowl so the left wall (49637), base (49029) and right wall (47508) form a visibly rounded U under the rim star 49669. Keep the handle arch running from knob 50583/50564 down to apex 49583 and into rim 49669 with a clear gap from the bowl walls. Keep the spout tip 46774 at the upper right of the bowl, pointing outward, and hang the water drops 47205 and 47310 below it. Move labels so none overlap: put 'right wall of the bowl' below or to the right of star 47508 and 'spout lip tip' above or right of 46774. Fill or thicken the blue outline into a solid silhouette so it does not read as a copy of the gold lines.
